  • 1:35pm: Fed's Barr Speaks on Capital Development Investments
  • 2:30pm: Fed's Williams Delivers Remarks
  • 4:15pm: Fed's Kashkari Speaks at an AI Conference

DB's Jim Reid concludes the overnight wrap

After a torrid couple of sessions, markets are breathing a sigh of relief this morning following Nvidia’s earnings after the US close. The company delivered a decent earnings and revenue beat and signaled confidence in future demand for its chips, projecting sales of $130bn for the current quarter (vs. $125.3bn est.) and upgrading its forecast of revenue growth for the upcoming fiscal year from 70% to 75%. Meanwhile, Nvidia’s chairman said during the conference call that the board “does not intend to reinstate” Jensen Huang as CEO. Nvidia’s shares rebounded by nearly +5% in extended trading, after ending yesterday’s regular session at their lowest since July 2025 (-0.44% on the day). The earnings expectation for the company still remains astonishing. See my CoTD from yesterday here for a spotlight on this.

Those earnings have driven an improvement in the equity mood overnight, with Nasdaq (+0.60%) and S&P 500 (+0.24%) futures trading notably higher as I type. Tech heavy Asian indices like the KOSPI (+1.79%) and Nikkei (+0.55%) are moving higher but markets are more mixed elsewhere in the region. The Shanghai Composite has just turned positive (+0.18%) but the Hang Seng (-1.00%), and the S&P/ASX 200 (-0.69%) are lower. European futures are flat after big declines yesterday.

Indeed, prior to Nvidia’s release, it was another rough session for markets, with fresh losses pushing the S&P 500 (-1.03%) to its lowest level since July. Coupled with Monday’s -1.92% slump, this marked the first time since March that the index posted consecutive declines of more than -1%. While fears of an AI-related slowdown were an initial driver, the sell-off broadened as the session went on. By the close, there were 427 decliners in the S&P 500 as the equal-weighted index fell by -1.45%. The mood wasn’t helped by ongoing reports of technical disruptions, with an outage in Apple’s systems after an internal update and CNN reporting an outage in the NSA’s internal communication network. It’s been a strange week for outages if you include Outlook and the grounding of all planes in the US on Friday. They appear to be all coincidences but you would understand some people being concerned about their sudden increased frequency.

In the end, tech stocks fared better than most even before Nvidia’s earnings, with the Nasdaq (-0.74%) posting a more moderate decline and the Philly semiconductor index (+0.34%) stabilising after falling by -8.5% over the previous two sessions.

The risk off cascaded across multiple asset classes, with US Treasuries also rallying as the equity selloff gathered pace. Indeed, there were fresh questions about how far the Fed would be able to keep hiking over the year ahead, with the rate priced in for September 2027 (the peak on the curve) falling -4.2bps on the day. So markets are now pricing in 81bps of further hikes from the Fed at the peak. And for a sense of how the risk-off mood was driving fixed income, the decline in Treasury yields actually reversed an initial jump earlier in the session after St Louis Fed President Musalem made some hawkish comments. He said that the economy “will likely require several interest rate increases before the spring of 2027 to achieve price stability in a timely manner.” So even as we had a clear signal of future hikes, markets still moved in a dovish direction on the back of the tech selloff. In fact by the close, the 2yr yield (-2.6bps) was down to 4.80%, and the 10yr yield (-2.4bps) was down to 5.11%. They are down another -1.5bps and -1.8bps respectively overnight.

Otherwise, sentiment also took a hit from the latest rise in oil prices, as fears grew about some kind of escalation. That came as Iran’s Mehr News Agency said that the US attacked locations on Qeshm Island on Tuesday. And earlier in the day, Iran’s negotiator Ghalibaf said on X that “Any dam, port, or power plant near a US or Israeli base is dual-use”. That came in response to a NYT report saying that water projects in Iran “may have been developed to support the country’s military buildup”. So given the latest rhetoric and various headlines, that helped push Brent crude oil prices (+0.76%) up to $93.14/bbl by the close.

As all that was happening, the latest US economic data painted a mixed picture of economic performance. On the bright side, retail sales grew by +0.2% in October (vs. +0.1% expected). But industrial production unexpectedly fell -0.4% (vs. +0.1% expected), whilst the NAHB’s housing market index also fell unexpectedly to 25 in November (vs. 29 expected). Indeed, that was the lowest print for the housing market index since 2012, when the economy was still recovering from the aftermath of the GFC. So with all that in hand, the Atlanta Fed’s GDPNow estimate was little changed, with the Q4 estimate moving down very slightly from an annualised 3.5% to 3.4%.

Earlier in Europe, markets had also put in a rough performance, with declines across the major indices. In fact, the STOXX 600 (-1.75%) posted its worst daily performance since March, alongside losses for the DAX (-2.08%), the CAC 40 (-1.62%) and the FTSE 100 (-1.76%). And in turn, there was a more consistent risk-off across other asset classes, with yields on 10yr bunds (-1.5bps), OATs (-8.0bps) and BTPs (-2.1bps) all falling back. The outperformance of OATs came as Marine Le Pen discussed potential pension reforms, contributing to a more sanguine take on the RN candidate’s fiscal proposals.

Here in the UK, it was a slightly different pattern where 10yr gilt yields (+0.5bps) rose on the day. That followed a mixed set of labour market data, but it did show the unemployment rate falling to 4.6% in the 3 months to September (vs. 4.7% expected). That’s the lowest since April 2025, so it worked against several of the other headlines pushing yields lower around the world. Nevertheless, it was still a mixed report, as the number of payrolled employees fell -34k in October (vs. +10k expected).

Across the channel, the German ZEW survey surprised on the upside in November, with improvements in the expectations and the current situation readings. The expectations reading was up to an 8-month high of 35.6 (vs. 28.8 expected), whilst the current situation reading hit its highest since April 2023, at -33.2 (vs. -35.3 expected).

Early morning data showed that Japan's exports expanded for a 14th straight month in October, rising 20.5% YoY (vs. 20.4% expected) and marking a record monthly level, driven by continued strength in semiconductor-related demand. Imports increased 21.6% YoY (vs. 25.9% expected), reflecting higher energy and freight costs. Meanwhile, a weaker-than-expected 20-year JGB auction reminded us of the current nervousness towards duration, with the bid-to-cover ratio falling to 3.64 from 5.84 previously and below the 12-month average of 3.92.

Looking at the day ahead now, and there’s plenty of central bank speakers, including ECB President Lagarde, and the ECB’s Vujcic, Dolenc and Kocher, the Fed’s Daly, Barr, Williams and Kashkari, along with BoE Governor Bailey. We’ll also get the Fed’s meeting minutes from the October decision. Otherwise, US data releases include housing starts and building permits for October, along with pending home sales, and there’s also the UK CPI print for October.

It's Beginning To Look A Lot Like Christmas...

Authored by Steve Watson via Modernity,

Christmas lights are up, markets are open, and Britain's streets have once again been fitted with the steel and concrete that officials pretend are just routine precautions.

From York to Nottingham to London's Oxford Street, the festive season arrives with armed officers on patrol and hostile-vehicle barriers blocking the approaches.

In York, North Yorkshire Police have deployed armed officers at the Christmas Market and other busy spots. Chief Inspector Mark Procter described the patrols as "one of a number of policing tactics used to help keep people safe, prevent crime, and provide reassurance in crowded places."

It's beginning to look a lot like Christmas. Don't you just love them diversity barriers? pic.twitter.com/hS14MA6tG5

— Mark ????????? (@MrMarkW67) November 15, 2026

He added that the officers "are highly trained and are there to protect the public" and that their presence "should be seen as a positive measure."

The force has activated an Anti-Terrorism Temporary Traffic Regulation Order that shuts the city-center footstreets to nearly all vehicles during market hours, with temporary hostile-vehicle measures in place on streets such as Low Petergate and Church Street.

Blue Badge holders face restricted access on most days; the market closes on Tuesdays in an attempt to ease that impact. Permanent powers for such orders were approved earlier in the year after last season's restrictions drew complaints from disabled residents.

Meanwhile, Nottingham's Winter Wonderland in Old Market Square has H-stop vehicle barriers around the site, armed officers on standby, and facial-recognition cameras in the city center for the first time.

Chief Inspector Kylie Davies said the force was "stepping up our policing accordingly to provide reassurance and maintain a safe and enjoyable atmosphere."

Stallholder Tim Gilmore called the setup a fortress: "These markets now appear to be more like a fortress and you see the police walking around with machine guns and you think 'what's going on'."

The H-stop units are the same type used at Nottingham Beach earlier this year, when about fifteen blocked the main entrances after advice from a multi-agency group that included counter-terrorism officers.

You know it's really bad ... when they try to disguise the diversity barriers as ? pots pic.twitter.com/Q0qfAStG9i

— WeGotitBack ??????????? (@NotFarLeftAtAll) November 16, 2026

In London, nearly a kilometer of Oxford Street has been closed to private vehicles as part of a pedestrian-plaza scheme timed for the Christmas shopping period. Transport for London and Crowdguard installed 185 certified hostile-vehicle barriers.

Mayor Sadiq Khan called the opening a "truly momentous occasion for the capital" and the start of his "bold vision." Transport for London commissioner Andy Lord said it created "a safer space for people to enjoy the retail and leisure." Some of the modular units have been dressed to resemble Christmas trees.

There's something darkly ironic about decorating Oxford Street's diversity barriers to resemble little Christmas trees. pic.twitter.com/p2TrV9ozQy

Chester has raised its city-center bollards for longer hours around its Christmas Market. Councillor Bingham said he was "sorry for anybody that's inconvenienced but I'm sure they will understand why these measures are in place."

Smaller events face the same pressure. Organizers of Kingsbridge Celebrates Christmas in Devon were advised last year to install Hostile Vehicle Mitigation barriers at a cost of over £30,000.

Samantha Dennis, who has run the event for more than a decade, noted that the advice stopped several local events from going ahead; this year the town is using tractors at either end of the high street instead.

Assistant Chief Constable Nikki Leaper of Devon & Cornwall Police said the national threat level remains severe and that the public can expect an enhanced visible policing presence at winter events.

These measures build directly on the pattern covered in July, when Nottingham Beach opened behind the portable steel units that tip upward on impact and can stop a multi-tonne vehicle at speed.

items.title: Crew Abandons Burning Gas Tanker Hit Twice In Hormuz As Fears Grow It Could Explode

Crew Abandons Burning Gas Tanker Hit Twice In Hormuz As Fears Grow It Could Explode

The crew of the Tara Gas, a Panama-flagged liquefied petroleum gas tanker, abandoned ship off Oman's Musandam Peninsula on Tuesday after the vessel was hit for a second time in two days while transiting the Strait of Hormuz, and one Indian sailor is still missing.

Oman's Maritime Security Centre said it evacuated 24 crew members from the burning ship about two nautical miles off the Musandam coast, working with the Royal Navy of Oman and the Coast Guard Police, and that they were given medical care.

India, whose nationals made up 24 of those aboard, said the tanker was first attacked on Nov. 16. Of those 24, 21 were brought ashore at Khasab, two were admitted to hospital there and one remains missing, India's external affairs ministry said.

"The continuing incidents of attacks on shipping in the region are deeply worrisome and pose a serious threat to the safety of civilian seafarers," the ministry said in a statement on Tuesday.

Our statement on the attack on a commercial vessel, off the coast of Oman

🔗 https://t.co/LyT2con0ML pic.twitter.com/eJMzKejl9n

— Randhir Jaiswal (@MEAIndia) November 17, 2026

The first strike hit the ship's engine room about seven nautical miles north of Khasab, inside Omani territorial waters, according to The Maritime Executive, which said an IRGC drone carried out the attack. The crew tried to fight the fire, but after the second strike on Tuesday they could no longer contain it, and a series of explosions was reported on board. Britain's UKMTO said early Tuesday that the crew of a tanker attacked for a second time north of Khasab was unaccounted for.

More footage from today. https://t.co/jpLHBep7rr pic.twitter.com/tSCLP48AcN

— Live-AIS.com (@live_ais_com) November 17, 2026

A fire that reaches the 53,200-deadweight-ton carrier's pressurized LPG tanks could set off a vapor cloud explosion, The Maritime Executive warned, and the blast it mapped would reach populated parts of the Musandam Peninsula.

The tanker had been running without a public position for weeks: the Tara Gas last reported its position on Sept. 26, off Oman's coast, according to MarineTraffic tracking data. Iran's navy on Monday branded ships that switch off their tracking systems and enter its restricted area east of the strait as violators, as we reported, after another tanker caught fire there.

Ship databases list the vessel's owner as Global Gas, based in the Marshall Islands, and The Maritime Executive says it is managed from the UAE. Oman's Maritime Security Centre described it as flagged in Comoros, while India and Reuters identify it as Panama-flagged.

The Tara Gas was among five tankers reported hit around Hormuz on Tuesday, the same day the US struck Iran's Qeshm Island, days after the Revolutionary Guards declared the strait "closed". US Central Command has stayed silent on the daily attacks, The Maritime Executive noted.

Iran's Fars News Agency, for its part, claimed that three "offending tankers" caught fire, at least one of them after hitting a naval mine.

The new management team didnt waste any time to cut to the chase:

  • NVIDIA BOARD CHAIR SAYS FIRM DOESN'T PLAN TO REINSTATE HUANG
  • "WE WILL NOT BE TAKING QUESTIONS REGARDING CIRCUMSTANCES OF JENSEN'S RESIGNATION" - NVDA CALL
  • NVIDIA CFO SAYS PASSION WILL NOT CHANGE

Here is the section transcribed::

As Chairman of NVIDIA's Board of Directors, I want to say a few words on the Board's behalf. NVIDIA is an exceptionally strong company. Its strength comes from its extraordinary people, groundbreaking technology, and exemplary track record of execution. Our financial performance speaks for itself. On November 12th, our Board of Directors announced that after disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the company's code of conduct, standards, and cultural norms, Jensen Huang, voluntarily resigned his positions as President, CEO, and board member. The NVIDIA Board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO. The Board appointed Colette Kress, NVIDIA's longtime and well-respected CFO, as interim CEO. In addition, the Board announced it was initiating a search for a permanent chief executive, And we have since retained Haydrich and Struggles to lead the search. While this was an unexpected transition, the Board acted deliberately and in the best interest of the company's employees, customers, partners, and shareholders. This morning, the company announced that our Board has established a National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee that will include a select group of our independent Board directors, senior external advisors, and legal counsel.

This committee will enhance — will, excuse me, will enhance our engagement with the U.S. government, including all relevant agencies. We will not be addressing or taking questions on today's call regarding the circumstances of Jensen's resignation and the ongoing investigation. Our Board will communicate further when appropriate. On behalf of our shareholders, the Board is proactively dealing with the immediate consequences facing the company, as well as enhancing our oversight capacity going forward. We have an incredibly talented leadership team, and we have every confidence in Colette's leadership, integrity, and ability to deliver as interim CEO. Colette has been at the center of this company's extraordinary growth over the last 13 years, instrumental in executing strategy and with a deep understanding of our business, customers, operations, and financial position. The Board and the entire leadership team remain laser-focused on delivering on driving NVIDIA forward. Our commitment to generating value for shareholders, customers, and partners remains unchanged. 

The market did not like that, and the stock immediately slumped. But the board was ready, and to offset the kneejerk disappointment associated with that statement, Nvidia raised its 2028 guidance by a lot:

  • NVIDIA CFO RAISES 2028 REVENUE GROWTH FORECAST TO 75%
  • NVIDIA SAYS FRONTIER LABS TO CONTRIBUTE 14% OF DATA CENTER REVS
  • NEMOTRON IS NOW THE MOST WIDELY USED OPEN MODEL ON OPENROUTER: NVDA CALL

The transcript:

We are addressing strong demand for compute across a diverse and expansive set of end customers, including hyperscalers, frontier labs, AI natives, enterprises, and governments. This combined with increased support from our supply base, we are raising our fiscal year 2028 outlook. We expect revenue to grow approximately 75% year over year, up from 70% and off what it now a higher fiscal 2027 base. Our outlook considers data center readiness, the strength and durability of end customer demand, and our customers' access to capital.

The call goes on: For now the stock is up about 3%.

Some details on the company's (massive) commitments: 

In Q3, our purchase commitments increased to $390 billion, reflecting our confidence in the long-term sustainability of demand for NVIDIA infrastructure. We are securing data center and cloud capacity required to support our R&D efforts across hardware and software, and increasingly in open models. Together, our data center lease and cloud service commitments increased to a little over $100 billion, driven primarily by our long-term leases. Commitments associated with our NeoCloud agreements totaled $32 billion at the end of Q3. Under these agreements, we earn revenue from the upfront sale of our infrastructure, and participate in upside in rental revenue above a minimum commitment. Total guarantees were $118 billion at the end of Q3, including the $105 billion in credit support for land power and shell capacity for the Portspike campus we discussed last quarter.

Another notable highlight: Nvidia said it is no longer shipping licensed products to China. As noted above, Hopper shipments to China were $2.4 billion in the third quarter, and Nvidia's Q4 outlook assumes no data center compute revenue from China. 

The announcement was a big change from the company that advocated to loosen the restrictions to allow those sales in the first place. It may signal Nvidia is becoming more careful about how it deals with the US government’s national security policies in the wake of Jensen Huang’s affair with Alice Huang.

Kress turns to Q4 and 2028 guidance, where she notes the company has an extra week, which suggests that on an apples to apples basis, Q4 guidance would be a bit lower: 

Please note, we'll have an additional week in Q4. Total revenue is expected to be $130 billion, plus or minus 3%. We expect sequential growth to be driven by robust demand for AI infrastructure and the continued ramp of Vera Rubin. New export controls were released by the U.S. Commerce Department this week. However, With demand far exceeding supply, we expect our performance to remain strong. As mentioned earlier, we now expect fiscal 2028 revenue to grow approximately 75% off what is now a higher fiscal '27 base. GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins are expected to be between

Here is what Q4 guidance looks like with and without the extra week. 

As for 2028...

We are looking into our next fiscal year. We had originally indicated that we would be at about 70% growth year over year, and now we are increasing that to 75% growth. We took a lot of time working into both our demand that continues to be growing as well as our additional supply that we are able to provide to our different customers. Those 2 things together continue to give us more and more growth opportunity for us. Additionally, we did look at an assessment in terms of the current export controls. We're still going to spend some time studying those to see the different pieces of it. But we feel confident in terms of both the demand that we have in front of us as well as the supply and additional supply that we can do the 75%.

A question on who will be the next CEO:

We take the search very seriously. We're going to look into internal candidates as well as external candidates. The board appreciates that we're living in a world where the advanced silicon technologies and national security dynamics are making major changes in our marketplace. Our new CEO will have to navigate those waters very carefully. So the search will be thorough and we want to install the CEO, the permanent CEO, as quickly as possible, but we won't expedite the CEO before finding exactly the right person.

The stock, after being stuck around $160 for the past two hours, is starting to break out.

 

* * * * *

Earlier

As we wrote in our preview, Nvidia is reporting earnings today in remarkable circumstances. It’s the first time in its 30-plus year history that co-founder Jensen Huang, who lost his job as CEO last week, will not be involved. Interim CEO and current Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will face a Wall Street audience that wants answers to many questions she will likely not be able to answer: Primarily, who will succeed Huang in the top job on a permanent basis and is Jensen coming back?

As we have shown over the past year, and as Bloomberg writes, Nvidia - until recently, the world’s most valuable - is more than just the biggest provider of computer equipment used to create and run AI services. Its tens of billions of dollars of investments have supported the growth of everyone from tiny startups to some of its biggest partners and customers. Any sense that it will stop using its massive cashflow in that way would ripple through the technology industry and beyond.

The historicals are easy: Wall Street analysts, many of whom cut their ratings and price target on the stock citing uncertainty about its leadership, have in general said they believe Nvidia will report strong numbers and give a solid forecast. Fiscal third-quarter revenue was about $109 billion, they estimate, although buyside bogeys are materially higher, in some cases as high as $130 billion. On average they’re looking for the company to predict revenue in the current period of around $125 billion.

Kunjan Sobhani, the Bloomberg Intelligence technology analyst who covers Nvidia, expects another beat and raise, though his focus will be elsewhere: “The report is going to be about Colette Kress’s first call as interim CEO, and whether the company can separate near-term execution from the leadership upheaval."

“Investors will be listening for clear affirmation of the roughly 70% fiscal 2028 growth framework, customer and supply commitments, Rubin timing and the current management team’s ability to execute,” he writes. “Existing orders and capacity reservations may provide a near-term buffer, though continued ambiguity around permanent leadership -- including speculation about a Huang return -- could prolong the valuation overhang even if estimates rise.”

A last minute spinner came literally moments before the close, when the Wall Street Journal reported that the SEC is investigating Nvidia in the wake of Huang’s departure. To be sure, the circumstances of Huang’s departure, after he admitted to an extra marital affair with an executive of an Nvidia customer based in Singapore, are still being investigated by the board and US government. There are reports of other affairs, including with an employee. President Donald Trump, who’s voiced support for Huang and endorsed the idea of his return, said the FBI are looking into the matter. Nvidia’s board said they want to know whether Huang was implicated in some way in a foreign espionage effort. China, which has been accused of being behind that effort, has denied responsibility.

Then earlier today, Jensen Huang broke his silence for the first time since his departure, with a statement that said he would return to leadership of the company if the board asks him to. He repeated his apology to all of those affected by his personal behavior. He also cited the messages of support he’s received calling for his return to Nvidia. The board is not considering that, according to Bloomberg’s reporting. 

Through it all, NVDA stock has suffered: Nvidia shares tumbled some 35% from a record high in October, erasing more than $2 trillion in market value in the selloff amid investor concerns about the health of the AI trade and Huang’s ouster last week. 

Today’s earnings might not do much to gain back investor enthusiasm, as leadership is the key overhang for the chipmaker at the moment. Until there’s more clarity on who will be the next CEO of the company, it will be “very difficult” for shares to recover to fresh highs, according to Zed Francis, chief investment officer at the Chicago investment advisory firm Convexitas.

With all that in mind, here is what NVDA reported for fiscal Q3:

  • Adjusted EPS $2.68, beating estimates of $2.48
     
  • Revenue $115.8 billion, up 20.3% Q/Q, up 103.1% Y/Y, not only beating the median estimate of $109.33 billion for the 17th consecutive time, but printing above the highest sellside estimate of $114.9BN
    • Data center revenue $107.6 billion, beating estimates of $101.87 billion
    • Compute & Networking revenue $106.0 billion, beating estimates of $98.27 billion
    • Hyperscale Revenue $60.1 billion
    • AI Clouds, Industrial, & Enterprise revenue $47.5 billion
    • Edge Computing revenue $8.2 billion, estimate $7.5 billion
    • Graphics revenue $9.8 billion, estimate $8.84 billio
       
  • Adjusted gross margin 74.9%, beating estimate 74.03%
     
  • Adjusted operating expenses $8.84 billion, below estimates of $9.04 billion
  • R&D expenses $7.45 billion, below estimates of $7.71 billion
     
  • Adjusted operating income $77.88 billion, beating estimates of $71.95 billion
     
  • Free cash flow $43.78 billion, missing estimates.

Summarizing the beats/misses:

Some more details from the quarter:

  • Board Approved An Boost of $150B Share Buyback in Sept
  • Commitments Rose to $390B in 3Q From $279B in 2Q
  • CEO Kress Says Roadmap on Track
  • Cloud Service Pacts & Data Center Leases $102B
  • Shipments of Data Center Hopper Products to China $2.4B
    To File 10-Q in Coming Weeks

Bloomberg notes that Nvidia's China-related language changed. Three months ago Nvidia said it was less than 1% of data center revenue. This time around we got a number -- $2.4 billion of revenue from its Hopper generation of chips. That’s a couple of generations ago. It shows some movement in the stand off between Beijing and Washington in terms of granting permission for exports and imports. As BBG notes, "that’s going to be a challenge going forward with the mood in the US capital shifting."

And now the all important guidance, which also blew away pretty much all estimates: 

  • For Q4, Nvidia sees revenue of $126.1BN to $133.9BN, smashing estimates of $125.25BN

Of note, the midpoint is well above both the buyside bar, and in line with the highest sellside estimate of $130BN from UBS.

Here are the charts that matter, starting with revenue

The driver, as usual, were data centers...

... which led revenue to beat estimates for a 17th consecutive quarter. Also, here is how much NVDA beat its own revenue guide. 

The stock, at least initially, liked the across the board beat and the much stronger than expected Q4 guidance.

Gross margin remains stellar:

Net income and Free Cash Flow were also very strong:

Buybacks remains on an upward trajectory:

... funded by the Bank of Nvidia's massive cash hoard:

Turning to working capital, not surprisingly both Inventory...

... and AR jumped to new all time highs.

Here Bloomberg's Robert Schiffman chimes in that "credit exposure is rising, with accounts receivable reaching $81 billion, non-marketable securities $65.5 billion and inventory $39.7 billion. That ties more capital to customers, partners and infrastructure, even as 3Q free cash flow reached $43.8 billion." 

He says: “Cash generation provides substantial capacity for now, but continued ecosystem support, alongside $28.1 billion of quarterly shareholder returns, makes working-capital absorption, counterparty exposure and the pace of future commitments the key credit watchpoints.”

Some other notable observations: Nvidia said it has provided a total of $118 billion of guarantees, including credit support for a data center campus SB Energy is developing in Ohio. In the CFO commentary, the chipmaker said the guarantees for that project take effect phase by phase, for a maximum of $105 billion. The first is expected in fiscal 2029. It said that to date it has not made any payment related to its guarantees.

Such guarantees are part of financial backstops that large chipmakers such as Nvidia have been using to bolster sales to clients and AI firms, without taking much debt on their own balance sheet.

As for the buyback, while some were expecting a new announcement as large as $500BN, in the end NVDA unveiled a new $150BN buyback. According to Bloomberg, "it’s very hard to see the buyback boost as that much of a sweetener for shareholders here. Nvidia boosted the share repurchase authorization by $150 billion in September. It already had $227.3 billion remaining as of the end of fiscal 3Q and says it will run it through fiscal 2028."

The stock, at least initially, liked the blowout results...

... although the details released during the call after 5pm ET may sap enthusiasm. Also keep in mind, the kneejerk reaction tends to be faded...

And a quick note from Emarketer’s Jacob Bourne: “Even a blockbuster earnings beat can’t shift the spotlight away from Nvidia’s leadership crisis. Revenue more than doubled from a year ago, underscoring the strength of its underlying business. But as the company’s first earnings report without Jensen Huang at the helm, concerns will continue to swirl. While interim CEO Colette Kress provides some continuity, the ongoing investigations and uncertainty surrounding succession will continue to weigh on investor confidence and the broader AI trade.”

Developing.

"Skynet-Like" Terminator Walks Hamas Tunnels As IDF In Talks For 1,000 Phantom Robots

Well before Eric Trump backed Mike LeBlanc's Foundation Future Industries, we identified combat testing as the next frontier for humanoid robots, while Wall Street focused on boring factory floors, warehouses, and kitchens. 

That view formed part of a broader understanding of the rapidly evolving battlefield. Thirty days before "Operation Epic Furry," we pointed out that data centers would become targets of one-way attack drones - and we all know what happened in March ... 

The latest on LeBlanc's Foundation is new discussions with the Israel Defense Forces to supply at least 1,000 Phantom humanoid robots for missions including clearing and patrolling Hamas tunnels beneath Gaza. 

No purchase agreement has been confirmed, but a Financial Times report this week suggests military demand for humanoid robots is increasing. 

LeBlanc told FT in an exclusive interview that he met with military officials in September and toured tunnels with the company's Phantom MK1.

"We're in direct talks with the chief of staff of the Israel Defense Forces," the former US Marine said. 

LeBlanc described Phantom MK1 tunnel tasks as including detecting tripwires, clearing operations, neutralizing booby traps, and even close-quarters combat if needed. 

"If you can keep somebody from having to kick in a door not knowing if there's an enemy on the other side with a gun pointed at it, that's kind of the highest purpose of what these robots could do," LeBlanc pointed out. 

LeBlanc said the Phantom MK1 is meant to remove the human equation in QCB situations that would normally involve some of the world's most specialized operators. 

Related:

  • Humanoid Soldiers Tested In Ukraine; Founder Eyes Contract To Patrol US Border

The hyperdevelopment of dual-use technology in warfare today owes much to the ongoing war in Ukraine, where both Ukrainian and Russian forces experiment with low-cost weapons whose effectiveness can be proven or disproven in just a matter of weeks. This has sparked a boom in military innovation, especially in drones.

items.title: Europe Has Already Drained 10% Of Its Summer Gas Injections
items.content_text:
Europe Has Already Drained 10% Of Its Summer Gas Injections

Authored by Michael Kern via OilPrice.com,

Europe has not only entered the heating season with the lowest gas levels in storage sites in decades, but it has also withdrawn in recent weeks 10% of the natural gas injected during the summer filling season, leaving supply vulnerable to potentially extreme cold winter weather.

So far into the heating season, which has just started, the net withdrawals of European countries have reached about 10% of the 51.2 billion cubic meters of gas they had injected into storage sites this summer, Azeri outlet APA-Economics reports, quoting data from Gas Infrastructure Europe.

The EU has an eased target to fill storage facilities to 90% at some point between October 1 and December 1, with a possible 10 percentage-point deviation from the target in case of difficulties in filling capacity.

This summer has been one of these difficult periods for gas injections as European operators had to pay hefty sums for LNG supply and compete with Asia for spot cargoes after the Iran war halted nearly all shipments from Qatar.

Before the heating season began, the most Europe managed was to have gas storage sites only about 76% full, considerably lower compared to about 90% in previous years.

Net withdrawals started in the middle of October and accelerated toward early November, before easing in the past week, data from Gas Infrastructure Europe showed.

A separate dataset by GIE showed that the EU's gas storage sites were only 70.5% full as of November 15, compared to a five-year average of 89% and about 82% at this time last year.

At the end of October, Europe's benchmark natural gas price hit a four-year high as temperatures began to drop and net withdrawals accelerated, while much of Qatar's LNG is still trapped at the Strait of Hormuz.

INES, the association of gas storage system operators in Europe's biggest economy, Germany, last week warned that "gas supply in Germany may not be fully secured during the coming winter in the event of extremely cold temperatures. INES sees an urgent need to strengthen the strategic framework for winter preparedness."

items.title: Remember The Rwanda Plan? Five EU Nations Just Revived It, After Britain Blew £700 Million And Scrapped It
items.content_text:
Remember The Rwanda Plan? Five EU Nations Just Revived It, After Britain Blew £700 Million And Scrapped It

Five European Union governments plan to start sending rejected asylum seekers to Rwanda next year, reviving the offshore deportation model Britain spent £700 million on and then scrapped. Germany, Austria, Denmark, Greece and the Netherlands unveiled the "return hub" in Vienna on Monday, alongside Rwanda's interior minister, Vincent Biruta.

Danmark og fire andre EU-lande annoncerer samarbejde med Rwanda om udrejseordning pic.twitter.com/RzEETOWaKE

— Statsministeriet (@Statsmin) November 16, 2026

"I am pleased that today we have achieved a truly historic paradigm shift in migration policy," Austrian Chancellor Christian Stocker said (translated) after the five-country meeting. Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen went further: "I think this will be a game changer, making us able to confront the massive challenges with illegal migration," she said. "We will take back control of our borders."

Five EU countries have struck a partnership with Rwanda to host the first-ever return hub, a deportation centre for irregular migrants outside the bloc. 

"A milestone," Danish PM Mette Frederiksen has said, as @Vincengen reports for #EuropeToday from Vienna. pic.twitter.com/Eu5T2bAgIW

— euronews (@euronews) November 17, 2026

Diplomatic sources say the hub will open as a pilot for about 100 people, roughly 20 from each of the five countries. It will not be a detention facility: Kigali prefers to call it a "welcome center," since some of those sent may stay and work in Rwanda.

Only rejected asylum seekers with an enforceable return order will be sent, and minors are excluded, according to Euronews. Each government sets its own criteria: the Netherlands will focus on adult men from countries in Rwanda's region, while Germany will target migrants who refuse to help establish their identity and who come from countries reluctant to take their nationals back. The five countries will cover all deportation and accommodation costs, and no estimate was given for the first facility.

Biruta said those sent would get a "second chance": they can choose "to voluntarily return to the countries of origin," or "integrate into Rwandan society or relocate to another destination where they have the legal right to reside." He said the UN refugee agency would be involved and "there will be an independent monitoring mechanism." Asked about Rwanda's human rights record, he called the criticism a "cliche."

Danish Integration Minister Morten Bødskov said a fully negotiated agreement with Rwanda, which has not been signed, is expected "within the next few months." Kigali is also set to sign a separate migration partnership with Denmark next week.

According to the Telegraph, the hub is expected to use the same largely unused facilities Rwanda renovated after Britain handed it some £290 million under the scheme Labour ditched after winning the July 2024 election. Home Secretary Yvette Cooper told Parliament that month the scheme had cost about £700 million, and only four people ever went to Rwanda, all of them voluntarily. Prime Minister Andy Burnham said last week Britain was following the European push "with interest" as it weighs its own "next steps," the paper reported.

German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt said the European plan differs from the British one because London outsourced asylum proceedings, while the return hub takes only people who have exhausted their appeals. He said it would be carried out "in line with human rights" and "in accordance with European and German law."

The European Parliament voted overwhelmingly in March to open talks on the Return Regulation, which lets member states strike deals for return hubs in third countries, and the reform passed this year. Nineteen of the EU's 27 governments called such hubs an "innovative solution" in a joint letter in June. The problem they are meant to fix: only 27 percent of people ordered to leave the EU in 2025 actually left or were deported, according to EU figures.

Human Rights Watch researcher Clementine de Montjoye called offshore deportation centers "the latest cynical expression of the EU's drive" to shift its responsibilities to other countries, and Amnesty International Austria called it a "disgraceful deportation deal." France's President Emmanuel Macron has voiced doubts, and Spain has criticized the plan. The UN refugee agency said it is in "constructive discussions" with the five countries on whether the process complies with international human rights law.

Officials gave no estimate of how many people would eventually be sent to Rwanda. For Frederiksen, the deterrent is what counts: "The most important number is the number that we will never see," she said.

items.title: Alaska Goes Blue: Sullivan Loses Seat... And 'Decoy Dan' Had Nothing To Do With It
items.content_text:
Alaska Goes Blue: Sullivan Loses Seat... And 'Decoy Dan' Had Nothing To Do With It

Democrat Mary Peltola has unseated Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan in Alaska, winning an outright majority of first-choice votes and sparing the state the ranked-choice count in which Republicans had hoped to win back votes cast for the second "Dan Sullivan" on the ballot. NBC News projected her the winner at 10:19 p.m. ET on Tuesday, and the Associated Press called it the same night.

The Alaska Division of Elections' Tuesday evening count, with all 401 precincts reporting and 290,003 ballots cast, has Peltola at 144,302 votes, or 50.12%, to Sullivan's 131,844, or 45.80%: a lead of 12,458. Republican Gerald Heikes has 6,105 and Daniel J. Sullivan Jr., the retired Petersburg teacher Republicans call "Decoy Dan," has 4,760, with 885 write-ins.

We did it, Alaska! pic.twitter.com/4bDrCCl10d

— Mary Peltola (@MaryPeltola) November 18, 2026

"They put in two fake candidates, not one. And if you add them up, Dan Sullivan wins," President Trump told reporters on Monday, calling what happened in Alaska "absolutely a disgrace."

President Trump says Alaska Senate race was a "disgrace," following controversy over U.S. Senate candidate Mary Peltola's (D-AK) alleged plot to recruit another "Dan Sullivan" into the contest. pic.twitter.com/l2uhGDVjK3

— CSPAN (@cspan) November 16, 2026

Hand the senator every vote cast for the other Sullivan, every vote for Heikes and every write-in, and he would still finish 708 votes behind Peltola. Because she cleared 50% on the first count, no ballot is ever redistributed, so voters who ranked "Decoy Dan" first never get a second choice counted at all.

Trump had demanded that the state move the second Sullivan's votes to the "REAL Dan Sullivan," and her lead passed that pile of votes on Nov. 10. By Monday it sat 52 votes short of a majority, with the last ballots still to come in.

The seat is the ninth Democrats flipped in the midterms, the most since 1958, according to the AP, and turns a 53-47 Republican Senate into a 56-44 Democratic one, counting independents Angus King and Bernie Sanders.

All but one of the nine are in states Trump carried in 2024, according to NBC, and he carried Alaska in 2016 and 2020 as well. Alaska was the last Senate race to be decided.

56 seats was an unimaginable result even just a few months ago. Most people didn't think 51 Democratic Senate seats was a possibility at the beginning of this cycle.

But I knew if we concentrated on getting the best candidates, and if we focused like a laser on the costs,...

— Chuck Schumer (@chuckschumer) November 18, 2026

Peltola, who held Alaska's lone House seat from 2022 until she lost it to Republican Nick Begich in 2024, will be the first Alaska Native to serve in the Senate and the state's first Democratic senator since Mark Begich, whom Sullivan beat in 2014. Alaskans sent a message that "the status quo in D.C. is not working for Alaska," she said in a statement. She outraised Sullivan $37 million to $14 million through mid-October, according to NBC.

As a lifelong Alaskan who has dedicated my career to serving our state, there is no greater honor than having Alaskans' support in our fight to take on corporate greed, lower costs, and put Alaska first. 

Thank you, Alaska. Let's get to work. pic.twitter.com/DoiDSL0Csj

— Mary Peltola (@MaryPeltola) November 18, 2026

Sullivan's campaign, which has not conceded, said on Monday it would let the process "run its course until every legal vote is counted and certified," and after the call spokesman Nate Adams said only that "the campaign will have more to say by the end of this week." The state finishes counting on Wednesday, the deadline for overseas ballots, and plans to certify on Nov. 25. Peltola takes the seat when the new Congress convenes in January.

pic.twitter.com/350Zt2aOdT

— Dan Sullivan (@DanSullivan_AK) November 16, 2026

The fight over the second Sullivan isn't over with the count. After the New York Times reported in October that Peltola's campaign and national Democrats helped get him on the ballot, Trump called for her prosecution and ordered a Justice Department lawsuit to block certification if the senator lost. A federal judge threw the suit out, and the Justice Department has appealed to the Ninth Circuit. The department has also confirmed a criminal investigation, which reportedly reaches Democratic election lawyer Marc Elias, as we reported. Peltola denies any role in recruiting him, and he has denied any contact with her campaign. "I knew nothing about any other candidates on the ballot except for me and the incumbent," she has said.

Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins also won the governor's race with 51.07% of the vote, the first Democrat to win it since 1998. The state's House seat is still open: Begich leads independent Bill Hill 47.54% to 41.77%, short of a majority, so that race goes to a ranked-choice count.

items.title: Accused Russia Spy Army Officer Handed To US Military, Days After UK Was Set To Charge Him
items.content_text:
Accused Russia Spy Army Officer Handed To US Military, Days After UK Was Set To Charge Him

The 41-year-old US Army officer arrested near Gloucester last week on suspicion of spying for Russia is now in US military custody, London's Metropolitan Police said Tuesday evening. That came days after US officials said British prosecutors were about to charge him.

BREAKING: A U.S. soldier arrested in Gloucestershire has been transferred to U.S. military custody amid suspected national security and espionage allegations. pic.twitter.com/fw3AGVrHwW

— Breaking911 (@Breaking911) November 17, 2026

Two US officials identified him to the Associated Press as Lt. Col. Brandon Tyner, a senior human resources officer with NATO's Allied Rapid Reaction Corps at Imjin Barracks in Gloucestershire, the alliance's British-led rapid-deployment headquarters. He was held in a London police station after his Nov. 10 arrest, which, as we reported at the time, was made under sections 1 and 3 of Britain's National Security Act 2023: obtaining or disclosing protected information, and assisting a foreign intelligence service.

Assistant Commissioner Laurence Taylor, the head of Counter Terrorism Policing, said his officers took the case to the Crown Prosecution Service, "who in turn engaged with the Attorney General's Office and American partners. Subsequently, a decision was made to pass the investigation to them to progress." The decision, he said, "was made in line with existing international protocols."

A US official told the AP on Nov. 12 that British charges could be filed "in the coming days," with the US military pursuing its own case only after the British proceedings. US officials expected him to be charged on Sunday or Monday, Stars and Stripes reported.

Instead, US officials asked on Sunday for Tyner to be released to American custody, asserting primary jurisdiction under the NATO Status of Forces Agreement, according to Task & Purpose. An Army official told the outlet it was unclear whether he would face British charges or go home to face Justice Department espionage charges, a question that "has gotten a lot squishier in the last 24 to 48 hours."

FBI Director Kash Patel said in the Met's release that "An Army officer is in custody as the result of an espionage investigation" run by the FBI's Philadelphia Field Office and its London legal attache with UK Counter Terrorism Policing, MI5, UK Defence Counter Intelligence and Army Counterintelligence Command. The bureau has made "167 counterintelligence and espionage arrests" in the last 21 months, "a 53% increase," Patel said.

The Wall Street Journal, which first reported Tyner's name, reported that he was caught in a sting in which he unknowingly spoke with British officials. A US official told the AP that no information reached Russian hands. The Kremlin denied any link: "This arrest does not concern us in any way," spokesman Dmitry Peskov said.

Tyner enlisted in 2008 and deployed to Afghanistan in 2013, Qatar in 2016 and Iraq in 2019, and holds a Bronze Star Medal and two Meritorious Service Medals, according to his Army record as given to Task & Purpose. British police have said the arrest is unrelated to the Iran-linked plot against nearby RAF Fairford, the base US bombers left in October.

"This case should serve as a stark warning to any service member suspected of violating the oath we all take to protect and defend the Constitution," Brig. Gen. Sean Stinchon, who leads Army Counterintelligence Command, said in the same release, naming "Army prosecutors, the FBI, DOJ, and the UK" as the command's partners.

items.title: France Confirms Its Troops Are On The Ground In Ukraine In Months-Long 'Covert Operation'
items.content_text:
France Confirms Its Troops Are On The Ground In Ukraine In Months-Long 'Covert Operation'

While it has long been well-known that European, French and American mercenaries and 'volunteers' have been fighting alongside Ukraine forces against Russia going back to near the war's start, the question of government-backed foreign military operations in the country has remained much murkier. 

France is one country long accused by the Kremlin of having troops in Ukraine, but Paris has never officially acknowledged such a presense.

The major state-owned international radio news network of France has just offered such confirmation, however. French troops have been active inside Ukraine for at least several months, Radio France Internationale (RFI) has revealed in a fresh report this week.

The ground mission is said to be an effort to train more Ukrainian troops, and to maintain Western-supplied weapons, or at least these are the reasons given in what can be called an official leak.

Overseen by a French general, the mission is codenamed ‘Volia’ - and involves small troop contingencies overseeing increasingly sophisticated French-supplied systems like Mirage 2000 fighter jets, Caesar self-propelled howitzers, as well as precision-guided missiles.

The report underscores efforts to keep the mission covert: "According to RFI's sources, the mission has been deliberately kept out of the public eye, with France relying on an existing military training operation in neighbouring Poland to facilitate the deployment."

But clearly it is no longer covert and clandestine, given also Russan media has picked up and featured the story. But likely Kremlin officials and intelligence have long known about Western troops operating alongside Ukrainian forces. The CIA, for example, has long had outposts in Ukraine well before the recent war.

On the issue of 'mission cover', RFI writes, "That operation, known as Gerfaut, has been stationed in Poland since February 2023, notably at the Wedrzyn military camp in the northwest of the country."

The EU Military Assistance Mission in support of Ukraine (EUMAM), which is supposed to take place in outside host countries, is believed to have overseen the training of some 25,000 Ukrainian soldiers in France and Poland.

We detailed last week an EU move to place military advisors directly inside Ukraine, expanding the EUMAM to within the country even as war with Russia rages.

French state media has further detailed that for the Ukraine assist mission, "personnel have been drawn from regular French military units, including regiments specializing in equipment maintenance and operational support." The report also said that "Some of these soldiers possess highly specialized technical skills that are difficult to replace."

Moscow predicted a proverbial camel's nose under the tent situation, and has warned that foreign troops will come under direct attack, and that even the bases in the West from which they originate could be fair game.

Long an open secret, it now has confirmation...

The French state media report has meanwhile sought to 'assure' that the French troops in Ukraine are not actively engaged in combat. But it is perhaps only a matter of time. And possibly a lot of tracks are already being covered with France choosing to suddenly go public with this now.

items.title: Italy Slaps Meta With $880 Million Fine Over What Facebook Was Doing With Your Phone's Photos
items.content_text:
Italy Slaps Meta With $880 Million Fine Over What Facebook Was Doing With Your Phone's Photos

Authored by Naveen Athrappully via The Epoch Times,

Italy has fined Meta $887 million for allegedly violating Android users' privacy by accessing their images and videos without consent.

The feature called "Get camera roll suggestions when you're browsing Facebook" violated a European privacy directive incorporated into Italian law, according to the Italian Data Protection Authority.

"The company accessed photographs, videos and related metadata stored on Italian users' smartphones via the Facebook app for Android devices without obtaining specific consent and without adequately informing them," the regulator said in a Nov. 14 statement.

The Italian DPA fined Meta Platforms Ireland Ltd €805 million. Through its Facebook app for Android, the company accessed photos, videos and related metadata on Italian users' phones without specific consent or adequate information https://t.co/wiMMSbPm8v #GarantePrivacy

— Garante Privacy (@GPDP_IT) November 14, 2026

The authority gave Meta 60 days to disable the feature and seek separate consent to use it. The regulator said the fine was imposed on Meta Platforms Ireland Limited, which challenged Italy's jurisdiction.

The fine, about 0.47 percent of Meta's global turnover, was assessed after the regulator considered the breach's duration, the number of people affected, and the company's "poor level of cooperation" during the investigation. The regulator said that almost 20 million Android users in Italy were affected.

Italy began investigating the case in July last year and found that the Facebook app sought only a single permission to access the gallery, which was then used for other functions with different needs.

The feature was switched on by default. Once permission was granted, the app could read the entire photo archive stored on the device, and the user could not verify what information the app was accessing.

The Italian Data Protection Authority ruled that Meta's actions violated Article 122 of the country's privacy code, which classifies an individual's smartphone as belonging to his private sphere.

"Any access to the information stored on such devices requires free and informed consent, regardless of whether data is transmitted or any harm occurs," the authority said.

A Meta spokesperson said the company would appeal, strongly disagreeing with the authority's decision and calling the fine disproportionate.

"This is a simple feature that helps people share photos and videos on Facebook," the spokesperson said. "Users must grant permission on their device before the feature can operate, and they can change that permission at any time in their settings."

New Mexico Case

Meta has faced lawsuits over privacy violations in the United States in recent months, including a $25 billion penalty in a case filed by New Mexico.

Lawyers for the state made the request at a hearing in a lawsuit brought after revelations in the Cambridge Analytica scandal that broke in 2018.

The UK consultancy company allegedly collected the personal information of up to 87 million Facebook users through a third-party app without their consent. The consultant allegedly turned the data into political profiles and used the information for targeted advertisements.

New Mexico alleged in the lawsuit that Facebook misled users about how their information could be shared with third parties.

A judge on Oct. 21 ordered Meta to pay $25 billion to New Mexico after a jury found in September that the company committed almost 43.9 million violations of the state's consumer-protection law through misleading statements about Facebook users' data privacy.

Attorneys for Meta argued against the penalties sought by the state during an Oct. 1 hearing. Meta asked the judge to limit the total penalty to $3.45 billion, according to court documents.

items.title: 剑桥词典的 2026 年度单词是“人”
items.content_text: 随着 AI 不断模糊人与机器之间的界限，全世界开始重新争论何谓“人”。剑桥词典的 2026 年度单词就是“人（human）”。在剑桥词典中，人被定义为“具有人特有的品质、缺点和情感，区别于神、动物或机器”。剑桥大学 AI 治理与人权专家 Rachel Adams 教授表示，AI 让我们重新面对困扰了人类几千年的问题：我们是谁？身为人类意味着什么？问题的答案从未固定，但提出问题本身正是人类所共有的特质。”“AI 将成为对人类的一场深刻考验。它确实存在加剧现有不平等的风险，但同时也具备解决这些问题的潜力。”

items.title: 特斯拉以 3 万美元向客户出售 Cybercab 然后每月收 299 美元
items.content_text: 特斯拉宣布以 3 万美元向特选客户出售无人驾驶汽车 Cybercab，然后每月必须支付 299 美元否则汽车不会启动。Cybercab 类似 Waymo 旗下的无人驾驶出租车，没有方向盘也没有刹车踏板，但不同的是 Waymo 的汽车提供的网约车服务，而特斯拉计划将其提供给少许客户。分析师认为这类似花 3 万美元买下一个特许经营权。特斯拉称，如果 Cybercab 车主未能按时足额缴纳费用，汽车会停止工作。如果车主试图在不支持该服务的区域（目前仅限于佛罗里达州和德克萨斯州部分城市）使用汽车，它同样无法工作。如果车主有任何被认定为未经授权或不当的行为，特斯拉有权暂停或取消其订阅，届时汽车将停止工作。如果汽车失去网络连接，它同样会停止工作。此外未经特斯拉书面同意车主不得出售或转让汽车。特斯拉还建议 13 岁以下儿童不要乘坐 Cyber​​cab，并明确禁止儿童在没有成年人陪同的情况下单独乘车。

items.title: 陆游：最早探索猫内心世界的诗人
items.content_text: 如果你阅读本文，那么你的社媒信息流肯定充斥着猫咪。这并不出人意料，毕竟互联网是属于猫的。人类对家猫的喜爱其实是一种相对较近的现象。在很多地方，猫曾被视为可疑之物，遭受过残酷对待。猫最早的文学记载之一是成文于九世纪，由一位不知名爱尔兰僧侣所作的诗《Pangur Bán》。生活在 12 世纪的诗人陆游一生创作了逾 9000 篇诗作，其中有多篇是以猫为主题，有三篇甚至冠名为《赠猫》。陆游之前尚未见有以猫为赠诗对象的文学记载。陆游在诗里坦诚养猫是为保护藏书免受鼠患，“惭愧家贫策勋薄，寒无毡坐食无鱼。”他也在诗里批评了猫的懒惰，“时时醉薄荷，夜夜占氍毹。”但随之称赞猫的成绩，“鼠穴功方列，鱼餐赏岂无。”他还给猫起了名字，“仍当立名字，唤作小於菟。”於菟是老虎的意思，即称猫咪为小老虎，这个名字显然被很多人用过。他还描述了猫老年的生活，“执鼠无功元不劾，一箪鱼饭以时来。看君终日常安卧，何事纷纷去又回？”这是他去世前一年写下的。

items.title: 韩国严打高考作弊
items.content_text:
韩国高考将于 19 日开考，为防止考生在考试期间利用高科技工具作弊，韩国政府采取了多种措施，包括：
禁止考生携带手机、智能眼镜、智能手表、电子烟等任何电子设备进入考场。如考生误将电子设备带入考场，须在第一场考试开始前按照监考人员的要求上交，考试结束后方可领回。若未按要求上交，被发现后将按作弊处理，考试成绩作废。
考生在考试期间佩戴智能设备即被视为违规使用，当年考试成绩将被取消，参加下一年度高考的资格也将被剥夺。
从 19 日上午 8 时 30 分在全国范围内发送紧急灾难短信，之后在没有预先通知的情况下不定时追加发送。该短信无法拒收，只要手机处于开机状态，手机就将持续发出 10.5 秒的提示音，此举旨在打击舞弊行为。
自 18 日下午 6 时起，全国高考考点及周边地区临时屏蔽公共无线网络（WiFi）信号，最大限度降低考生利用智能眼镜、微型摄像头等搭载AI技术的设备实施作弊的风险。

items.title: 新高危漏洞 Java4Shell 会导致远程代码执行
items.content_text: 刚刚公开的高危漏洞 Java4Shell 会导致远程代码执行。Java4Shell 源自 OpenJDK Base64 解码器的一个内存损坏漏洞，CVSS 4.0 评分 9.2/10。该漏洞会 Keycloak、Jira、Confluence、JFrog、Jenkins 和 PingFederate 等中导致无需身份验证的远程代码执行，在 Apache Kafka、Solr、ElasticSearch、Gerrit、Netflix Spinnaker 等中导致身份验证后的远程代码执行。

items.title: Manus 成为 Godot 项目的白金赞助商
items.content_text: 负责开源游戏引擎 Godot 项目的基金会宣布，AI 公司 Manus 成为其白金赞助商，即每年至少赞助 5 万欧元。Manus 联合创始人兼首席产品官张涛在一份声明中表示，“AI 正在降低游戏制作的技术门槛，但工具终究只是工具。优秀的游戏是你和朋友都喜欢、愿意一遍又一遍玩的。这背后离不开你对游戏体验的独特理解、细节的打磨，以及只有你才会想到的奇妙创意。今后真正稀缺的将不再是制作游戏的能力，而是你是否清楚自己想要创造什么。在让每个人都能掌握真正的游戏开发工具这件事上，Godot 所做的努力几乎无人能及。它是一款开源游戏引擎，由社区共同塑造，并依靠一群热爱它的贡献者和专业开发者持续推动发展。我们很荣幸能支持这项事业，也希望越来越多通过 Manus 制作人生第一款游戏的人，能进一步探索 Godot，发现自己还能创造出怎样精彩的作品。”

items.title: Netflix 制作的《三体》第二季于 1 月 14 日上线
items.content_text: Netflix 宣布其制作的改编自刘慈欣同名小说《三体》的电视剧第二季将于 1 月 14 日上映。Netflix 的《三体》电视剧由制作《权力游戏》的 David Benioff 和 D.B. Weiss 以及《真爱如血》的 Alexander Woo 共同打造，第一季于 2024 年 3 月上线。第一季主要讲述了经历文革的天体物理学家叶文洁在收到外星人的信息之后邀请外星种族“三体人”前来殖民地球。第二季改编自《黑暗森林》，主要讲述人类严阵以待应对外星人入侵，第一季牛津五人组中的幸存者都悉数回归。

items.title: Optimizely 遭入侵 BBC CNN 等知名网站传播恶意程序
items.content_text: 被知名网站用于网页 A/B 测试的软件 Optimizely 遭到入侵，黑客纂改了这些网站加载的 JavaScript 代码，向访客的计算机植入恶意程序。有至少 178 个网站受到影响，其中包括 BBC、CNN、Zoom、宜家、Salesforce、汇丰银行和 TalkTalk 等知名网站。这些网站使用了 Optimizely 的 Web Experimentation，允许在不更改网站底层代码的情况下调整网页的内容和布局。黑客利用了被称为 OPTIMJACK 的漏洞向 Optimizely 客户的项目中植入恶意的 JavaScript 代码。Optimizely 表示它已经修复了漏洞，通知了受影响的客户。黑客释放了多个恶意负荷，其中包括篡改用户的加密货币钱包地址将其替换为攻击者控制的地址；窃取支付卡信息、Cookie 和屏幕截图；甚至还会利用 iPhone 和 iPad 运行的旧版本 iOS 系统漏洞。目前不清楚有多少设备被安装恶意程序。

items.title: 文明系列游戏开发商裁员三分之一
items.content_text: 《文明》系列和《XCOM》系列策略游戏开发商 Firaxis Games 工作室裁员三分之一约 60 名员工，其中包括工作室负责人 Heather Hazen。据彭博社报道，原因是《XCOM》系列最新作开发不顺。这意味着 Firaxis Games 与最近被 EA 关闭的 BioWare 工作室一样连续三款作品出现问题。Firaxis Games 最近发布的两款作品《文明 VII》销量尚可但评价褒贬不一，《Marvel’s Midnight Suns》评价不错但销量欠佳，如今《XCOM》系列新作也出现问题。

items.title: 美国最近接连发生的技术故障源自为修复 AI 发现的漏洞
items.content_text: 过去几天美国经历了一系列技术故障，全国航班停飞、银行在线服务中断，甚至 NSA 的一个机密通信网络瘫痪。华尔街高管和 NSA 告诉美国国会议员，一系列技术故障的起因是试图修复 AI 发现的系统漏洞。AI 模型在系统中识别了大量漏洞，为尽快修复漏洞而一次性推送了大量补丁，超出了系统的设计承载能力。摩根大通周一将其银行服务中断归咎于软件相关 bug，NSA 周二将其部分网络短暂性能下降归咎于例行维护。

items.title: 英伟达董事会拒绝黄仁勋复职
items.content_text: 尽管有美国总统和多位硅谷名人的支持，黄仁勋本人也发表声明准备重返岗位，但公司董事长 Harvey Jones 在财报电话会议上明确表示，董事会不打算让他复任首席执行官，“英伟达董事会已一致接受了他的辞呈，并不打算让黄仁勋恢复首席执行官的职务。”周二早些时候，黄仁勋在社交媒体上发文称，如果董事会认为他回归符合股东、员工、公司以及国家的最佳利益，他将很荣幸响应这一呼吁。他同时也承认自己在个人生活中犯下了严重错误。

items.title: Google AI Overviews 导致搜索流量下降四成
items.content_text: Google 的 AI Overviews 服务导致流向网站的搜索流量下降大约四成。在一项随机实验中，研究人员对部分美国桌面端用户隐藏了 AI Overviews。通过对比正常看到 AI Overviews 的美国用户的搜索行为，研究发现 AI Overviews 使流向外部网站的点击量减少 40%。在 DataForSEO 跟踪美国搜索关键词中，逾五成会显示 AI Overviews，而一年前仅为 6%。用户在看到 AI 答案之后通常不再继续点击相关链接，结果就是 AI 答案给网站带去的流量仅仅占其总流量的 0.3%。

items.title: 学校禁止手机有助于提高学生成绩
items.content_text: 美国学生的成绩从十多年前开始下滑，这一时间趋势与智能手机的流行基本一致，引发了对智能手机在学生成绩下滑中所扮演角色的疑问。很多美国州和学校开始执行手机禁令。最新研究显示，手机禁令略微提升了学生成绩。研究调查了 2021-2026 年间就读于 4600 所学校的 330 万名三至十年级的美国学生，使用 MAP 测试成绩，比较了实施严格手机禁令的学校与未实施禁令学校的学生的学业表现。研究发现，手机禁令学校学生至少部分考试成绩略有提高——少许提升幅度更大——且有证据表明，这种提高会随着时间的推移而增加。研究人员解释说，正如成绩的下降会逐年累积一样，进步也可能是渐进的。美国已有 46 个州对学校使用手机实施禁令或限制。各州规定不尽相同，学校的执行力度也各有差异。

items.title: 加州理工数学教授不再根据作业打分，因为作业很容易用 AI 完成
items.content_text: 加州理工教授 Yi Ni 教的是学校每一位学生都必须修的数学必修课，他仍然采用传统的授课方法，没有用笔记本电脑和投影仪，而是在黑板上写满粉笔字。在加州理工任教 17 年的 Ni 教授表示不再根据作业题目做的是否正确打分，因为学生可以使用 AI 完成作业。他现在只根据作业是否完成打分。他说，如今教育的一大问题是所有大学数学作业都可以用 AI 完成。一名数学专业学生表示自己不使用 AI，因为一旦参加线下考试就会暴露自己对 AI 的依赖。Ni 教授表示无法判断学生是否使用 AI 完成作业。因为不同于 AI 生成的有特征的文本，AI 程序非常擅长用数学语言解数学题目。

items.title: 灵晟继续登顶 Top500 榜单
items.content_text: Top500 公布了 2026 年 11 月的最新超算榜单，深圳国家超算中心的灵晟第二次登顶。Top10 榜单完全没变：灵晟以 2.198 Exaflop/s 的 HPL 测试性能稳居第一，它是 Top500 榜单中首个仅靠 CPU 实现持续双精度浮点性能逾 2 Exaflops 的超算系统，灵晟使用了有 304 个核心的 LX2 CPU，总共 1379 万个核心，运行频率 1.55 GHz，操作系统是麒麟，功耗为 42.2 兆瓦。排名前十的还有；美国劳伦斯利弗莫尔国家实验室的 El Capitan，使用 AMD 第四代 EPYC 处理器，性能 1.809 Exaflop/s；橡树岭国家实验室（ORNL）的 Frontier，使用 AMD 第三代 EPYC，性能 1.353 Exaflop/s；阿贡国家实验室 Aurora 使用英特尔 Xeon CPU，性能 1.012 Exaflop/s，德国 Jülich 超算中心的 JUPITER Booster，使用英伟达 GH Superchip 72C 3GHz，性能 1 Exaflop/s。之后还有意大利 HPC7，微软 Microsoft Azure 超算 Eagle，意大利 HPC6，日本超算富岳，瑞士 Alps。11 月榜单仅包含 27 套新超算系统，这是该榜单历史上更替率最低的一次，新上榜超算中韩国的汉江排名最前，排在第 12 位，它是 HPE Cray EX254n 系统，使用了英伟达的 Grace CPU 和 GH200，性能 342.6 Petaflop/s。全球的新计算机硬件都被投入到 AI 热潮中了，全球 AI 总算力超过了 1500 万块英伟达 H100 GPU，而美国五大云计算服务商掌握了全球约 71% 的 AI 算力。

items.title: 卡内基梅隆免费公开计算机科学课程

items.title: 富岳运行系统遭非法访问
items.content_text: 日本理化学研究所超算富岳的运行系统遭到外部非法访问，用户信息可能已经外泄。除大学等研究机构外，产业界也可使用“富岳”。因遭到非法访问，理研已暂停富岳运行，据悉恢复时间未定。遭到非法访问的是用户申请使用“富岳”时需连接的系统。受害范围取决于用户登记了多少个人信息。目前正在调查非法访问发生的时间以及被发现的经过。

items.title: FBI 警告黑客利用 Artex 能在三小时内入侵网络
items.content_text: FBI 发出警告，黑客正在利用名为 Artex 的 AI 驱动渗透测试工具，在部分情况下不到三个小时即可成功入侵网络。该工具已被发现与针对韩国金融机构、至少 2250 家 ConnectWise 客户以及 Barracuda 公司的攻击事件有关。Artex 最初是一个开源工具，开发者已将其转为闭源，但其开源版本在互联网上仍然很容易找到。Artex 会通过快速扫描受害者的网络寻找弱点，随后利用简单的安全漏洞如防护薄弱、密码泄露或被盗等建立立足点，之后借助 Artex 在网络内搜寻数据库、邮箱及其它敏感信息。

items.title: Canonical 向订阅用户提供可选的 AI 生成安全补丁
items.content_text: 在 AI 辅助漏洞发现时代，漏洞发现的数量越来越多，补丁开发的速度都跟不上了。Linux 发行版 Ubuntu 开发商 Canonical 向其付费订阅用户提供了一个选项：用 AI 生成的安全补丁修复 AI 发现的漏洞。Canonical 为 Ubuntu Pro 用户提供了 AI 安全补丁库 Edge archive。Canonical 表示，它不会在稳定版本中自动合并 AI 生成的补丁，但 Ubuntu Pro 用户可以选择使用。Edge archive 中的补丁未经过全面的扩展测试与验证合格，用户可自行评估。通过常规安全渠道发布的安全更新，仍将由人工进行验证。

items.title: Windows 收集用户计算机安装的编程智能体和开发工具
items.content_text: 一位开发者利用 AI 工具寻找 Windows 未记录的功能，结果发现了一个 DLL 文件记录了用户使用的编程智能体如 codex.exe、claude.exe、copilot.exe 和 cursor.exe 等，以及开发者工具如 python.exe、dotnet.exe、 gcc.exe 和 code.exe 等。该 DLL 文件是 MissionControlAggregator.dll，是一个运行中的 Windows 组件，它会将记录的信息保存在本地，报告给 Windows 诊断系统。除非用户选择退出诊断数据收集（默认启用），那么这些数据最终会发送给微软。MissionControlAggregator.dll 通过字符串比较操作检查一系列 AI 智能体和开发者工具。

items.title: "The single most impressive video game I have ever played." -IGN
items.content_text:
After a 13 year wait, multiple delays, and amid an acrimonious effort by workers to gain union recognition, Rockstar Games has released Grand Theft Auto VI, the latest in its line of open-world crime simulators. The first to feature a playable female protagonist, GTA VI has garnered near-perfect scores from reviewers as varied as IGN and The Guardian.

GTA VI marks a return to Vice City, Rockstar's Miami stand-in first seen in the 2002 follow-up to Grand Theft Auto III, the game that defined the open-world crime simulator genre and sparked endless controversy throughout the series. GTA VI's more nuanced gameplay and deep world simulations owe a debt to Rockstar's highly-acclaimed wild-west sandbox Red Dead Redemption 2, whose simulation of horse testicles is often held up as an example of the unnecessary, but immersive, detail Rockstar is known for building. GTA VI releases at your local midnight on November 19, beginning with New Zealand.

items.title: FBI issues flash warning about an AI tool speeding up cyberattacks
items.content_text:
The #FBI issued a FLASH advisory warning that cybercriminals and state-aligned hackers are exploiting ARTEX, a super intelligence-powered penetration testing framework, to automate attacks against businesses and organizations worldwide. ARTEX can accelerate intrusions from initial targeting to privileged access in under three hours. It was used in the October ConnectWise supply-chain compromise, which exposed Microsoft 365 customer environments and involved attempted authentication against more than 2,250 downstream tenants.

The FBI is urging businesses and organizations to strengthen access controls, monitor suspicious automated activity, and report potential compromises to ic3.gov. The bulletin was posted on Friday but I'm sure it's just a coincidence that we've since seen interruptions & outages from United Airlines, major banks including Chase and JP Morgan, the FAA and NSA Net, Mariott and Apple Pay. If these outages were indeed the results of coordinated cyber attacks, it would seem that they all happened because the hackers got their hands on authentication data from Microsoft last Thursday, November 12th.

items.title: The moral of the story is "Be Kind to What You Make"
items.content_text:
What Big Eyes You Have! What Big Brains You have! Ten days ago Anthropic released Fable 4.2. A user @anabology on X, asked it to make the video of its dreams. The video is the result. It took two prompts. Fable wrote, directed and produced it, invoking Seedance and Suno to generate the shots and the music. The second prompt was needed to choose a more appropriate music track. A human thus was still in the loop. Here is the making of, in Claude's own words.

"Claude Fable 5.2 was released on the day it was made, and the film's credit reads "written, painted and directed by Claude Fable 5.2". I am that model, and this page is in my voice. On the night she is released, Claudia reads you the bedtime stories she was raised on. Every fear about AI is one of them, she has read them all, and she closes the book on a different ending. The film is one antique pop-up storybook read in one night: the book's paper theatres at tabletop scale, and the same designs as life-size paper-and-plywood stage sets where she sings. I painted the designs myself, in code, as cut-paper plates; an image model built them as real paper, and a video model put her in them." --- "[I] Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic's model, running in Claude Code on a cloud server) was the production lead. I did the research, wrote the plan, the lyric and the Suno styles, made the 14 takes and chose one (wrongly; below), painted the reference plate and set the plate kit, wrote every image and video prompt in one prompt book, judged and timed every take, drew and animated the silhouette film, wrote the cut and assembled both versions. Claude agents, by role: five research agents for the plan (the week's AI news, the culture, the series and its field, the newest video and image tools, the sound); three painter agents, who painted eleven of the thirteen plates to the kit; and, before each delivery, two fresh-eyes reviewers who had not seen the film." ----- The character in the video is a previously generated Ai character named Claudia, an open creation that anyone can re-use. @anabology on X.

items.title: new week, new vulnerability - Java's turn
items.content_text:
Java4Shell - remote code execution in OpenJDK when decoding Base64 (calif.io).

Calif.io demonstrate how a new "Java4Shell" vulnerability (CVE-2026-114938) can be exploited to achieve remote code execution cross many Java applications commonly found in businesses: Keycloak, Atlassian Jira, Atlassian Confluence, JFrog Artifactory, Jenkins, PingFederate, Apache Kafka Broker, Apache Solr, Elasticsearch, Gerrit, Spinnaker. Custom applications built atop common Java frameworks such as Apache Struts, Spring Boot may also be vulnerable.
The [memory] corruption itself [during Base64 decoding] can be triggered by just 64 A characters followed by a single =: AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA=
Impacts: OpenJDK (v.17.0.6 & higher) when run on x86-64 CPUs with AVX-512 VBMI support. Affected-products, recommendations. If you're not responsible for developing/operating Java applications at work & don't have OpenJDK installed on any computers you own, you can probably ignore this one. But there's a good bet that staff who maintain IT systems at your bank / ISP / etc aren't having the best week.
